stem: A GP is helping a 13-year-old recover after major family stress; which single protective factor most supports adolescent resilience?

options.text: Avoiding all new challenges until life is calmer
Having one trusted adult who cares
Spending more time alone to build independence

explanation: Having one trusted adult who cares is the key protective factor for resilience. Supportive relationships help adolescents cope with stress and recover from adversity.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because resilience is supported by facing and adapting to adversity, not by avoiding all challenge.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a trusted caring adult provides emotional support, stability and a protective relationship that strengthens resilience.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because isolation is not a protective factor for resilience in adolescence.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because academic ranking is not the main protective factor identified; supportive relationships are more important.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because connection with peers is generally helpful rather than something to reduce.
